issues.title: Design question: the approved mannequin is a primitive placeholder, but the gate treats it as a hero asset that must reach 8.5
issues.description: This is a conflict between documents, raised before any picture exists; it is not an observation of the model. CLAUDE.md Part B Milestone 1 asks for 'a placeholder humanoid (mannequin) from primitives' and Milestone 12 replaces it with a proper enemy model. Verification/Config/targets.json lists the mannequin as tier 'hero' for M1, M2 and M12, and the gate passes a target only at 8.5. The Critic's instructions state that placeholder primitives belong in the 3 to 6 range however cleanly built. If the mannequin turns out to be what the design asked for, it probably cannot pass on modeling, cohesion and materials, and M1/M2 could not close their visual gate until M12. The Critic will not lower the standard or guess a score; Matthew should decide how the gate applies to an intended placeholder.
issues.reproduction: Read CLAUDE.md Part B section 15 (Milestones 1 and 12), the 'mannequin' entry in targets.json, and the 'Anchors' paragraph of orbital-critic.md side by side.
issues.expected: One stated rule for how a deliberately placeholder character is judged, decided by Matthew, before the first scored review.
issues.rootCause: The quality gate was added after Milestones 1-3 were designed around a placeholder character.
recommendedFixes: Matthew decides: keep the mannequin a hero target at 8.5 (so the placeholder must be replaced or lifted well above primitive shapes before M1/M2 can pass), or

Matthew decides: judge the mannequin until M12 only on animation, readability and technical soundness, with its art gate deferred to the M12 enemy model (a rubric or targets.json change only Matthew can make), or
Bring a real character model from the asset pipeline forward so the dismemberment system is reviewed on real art.
